review_locator: PMCID:PMC3777820, Eph/ephrin recognition and signaling review; PMCID:PMC3327877, Eph/ephrin cell-cell signaling review
primary_title: Repelling class discrimination: ephrin-A5 binds to and activates EphB2 receptor signaling
decision_basis: The reviews identify the cross-class ephrin-A5/EphB2 interaction; the cited primary study resolves a high-affinity EphB2-ephrin-A5 complex and shows receptor clustering, autophosphorylation, downstream signaling, growth-cone collapse and neurite retraction.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the unusual A-ligand/B-receptor cross-class topology, clustered/membrane ligand geometry and neuronal guidance context; no SCI transfer or ephrin reverse-signal claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3777820, Eph/ephrin recognition and signaling review; PMCID:PMC3327877, Eph/ephrin cell-cell signaling review
primary_title: Ephrin-B3, a ligand for the receptor EphB3, expressed at the midline of the developing neural tube
decision_basis: The reviews identify ephrin-B3 as an EphB3 ligand; the cited primary study characterizes murine ephrin-B3 and finds high-affinity binding to EphB3 among the tested Eph receptors, with midline neural-tube expression relevant to axon guidance.
limitations_preserved: Promote exact ephrin-B3/EphB3 binding and developmental guidance context only; receptor activation/forward signaling was not fully isolated in this paper, and no reverse or SCI claim is made.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3777820, Eph/ephrin recognition and signaling review; PMCID:PMC3327877, Eph/ephrin cell-cell signaling review
primary_title: Structural characterization of the EphA4-Ephrin-B2 complex reveals new features enabling Eph-ephrin binding promiscuity
decision_basis: The reviews identify the cross-class ephrin-B2/EphA4 interaction; the cited primary structural study characterizes the EphA4-ephrin-B2 complex and maps receptor-ligand binding determinants and affinity limits.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the cross-class EphA4/ephrin-B2 binding and low-affinity/oligomerization caveats; binding structure does not by itself establish a productive cellular relay or SCI function.
